Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the significant changes you're navigating as a new mother, and I'm here to support you every step of the way. As part of our conversation today, I'll be administering the EPDS, which is a tool that helps us understand how you're feeling and if there are any concerns that might need some extra attention.

The EPDS is designed to screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, and it's a valuable resource for us to better understand your postpartum experience. Please know that everything we discuss is completely confidential, and I'm committed to creating a safe, supportive space for you to share your thoughts and feelings. My goal is to provide you with a non-judgmental and empathetic ear, and to work together to identify any areas where you might need some additional support.

The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better sense of how you've been feeling over the past week. These questions are designed to be straightforward and easy to understand, and I'll be asking them in a way that feels conversational and natural. Don't worry if you're not sure about any of the questions - we'll take them one at a time, and I'm here to support you throughout the process.

So, let's get started. The first question is about how you've been feeling overall. I'd like to ask: Over the past week, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. to be honest, it's been a bit of a struggle lately. I mean, I do laugh and smile when my baby does something cute, but it's not as often as I used to. I just feel so tired and overwhelmed most of the time, and it's hard to find the energy to enjoy things like I used to. Even when I do laugh, it feels a little forced, you know? Like, I'm trying to be happy, but it's not really coming naturally. And sometimes, when I'm by myself, I just feel really sad and discouraged. It's like, I'm supposed to be happy and enjoying this new mom thing, but it's just not feeling that way. (pausing, getting a little choked up) Sorry, it's just... it's hard to explain. I just feel like I'm not doing this whole mom thing right, and it's really getting to me. (wiping away a tear)
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(sighing) Not as much as I used to, to be honest. I mean, I'll laugh at something my baby does, but it's not the same. I feel like I've lost my sense of humor a bit. Everything just feels so serious and overwhelming all the time. I'm constantly worrying about my baby's health, and if I'm doing everything right, and it's just... it's exhausting. (pausing, looking down) I don't feel like myself anymore. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, trying to survive each day. (voice cracking) Sorry, it's just... it's hard to explain. I feel like I'm failing somehow, like I'm not good enough for my baby. (fighting back tears)
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(shaking my head) Not really, lately. I mean, I used to love doing things like going out with friends, or trying new restaurants, or even just reading a book. But now, it all just feels like too much effort. I'm so tired all the time, and even when I do have some free time, I just end up worrying about my baby or feeling guilty about not spending enough time with her. (sighing) I don't really feel like I have anything to look forward to, to be honest. Every day just feels like a struggle to get through, and I don't really have the energy to enjoy anything. (pausing, looking down) It's like, I'm just going through the motions, you know? I'm not really living, I'm just existing. And it's hard, because I feel like I should be enjoying this time with my baby, but it's just not feeling that way. (voice barely above a whisper) I feel like I'm missing out on all the joy and happiness that I'm supposed to be feeling as a new mom.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Oh, yes... all the time. I feel like I'm always blaming myself for something. If my baby is crying, I think it's because I'm not doing something right. If she's not sleeping, I think it's because I'm not establishing a good routine. If she's not eating well, I think it's because I'm not making enough milk. (sighing) It's like, no matter what happens, I always think it's my fault. And it's not just the big things, it's the little things too. Like, if I forget to burp her, or if I don't change her diaper quickly enough... I just feel like I'm always messing something up. (shaking my head) And it's hard, because I know I'm trying my best, but it never feels like it's good enough. (voice cracking) I just feel like I'm failing her, and that's a really hard feeling to live with. (wiping away tears) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard to talk about this.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Yes, all the time. I worry about everything. Is my baby eating enough? Is she sleeping too much? Is she too hot or too cold? Is she developing normally? (taking a deep breath) I mean, I know it's normal to worry a little bit, but it feels like my mind is always racing with worst-case scenarios. I'll be sitting there, feeding her, and suddenly I'll think, "What if she chokes?" or "What if I drop her?" (shuddering) It's like, I know it's irrational, but I just can't seem to shake these thoughts. And it's not just during the day, either. At night, when I'm trying to sleep, my mind starts racing and I'll lie there for hours, worrying about all the things that could go wrong. (rubbing my temples) It's exhausting, both physically and mentally. And it feels like I'm always on edge, just waiting for something to go wrong. (sighing) It's hard to explain, but it's like I'm constantly walking around with this sense of dread, just waiting for the other shoe to drop.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, taking a deep breath) Yes... I've had those feelings too. It's like, my heart will start racing and I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me, and I'll think, "What's wrong? What's happening?" But then I'll look around and everything will be fine. My baby will be sleeping or playing, and my husband will be sitting there, looking at me like, "What's wrong?" And I'll be like, "I don't know... I just feel so scared all of a sudden." (shaking my head) It's really confusing, because I don't know what's triggering it. Sometimes it's when I'm alone with the baby, and sometimes it's when we're out in public. It's like, my mind is always on high alert, waiting for something to go wrong. (wrapping my arms around myself) And it's hard to explain, but it's like I'm always waiting for the other shoe to drop, you know? Like, I'm just waiting for something bad to happen, and that's making me feel really anxious and scared. (looking down, my voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm losing control, like I'm not able to take care of my baby or myself. It's a really scary feeling.
Things have been getting on top of me

(sighing, feeling overwhelmed) Yes... that's exactly how I feel. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. Taking care of the baby, keeping the house clean, cooking meals, paying bills... it's all just so much. And on top of that, I'm trying to recover from giving birth, and I'm not sleeping well, and I'm just feeling so tired and emotional all the time. (shaking my head) It's like, I feel like I'm drowning in responsibility, and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (looking down, feeling tears well up in my eyes) Sometimes I feel like I'm just barely holding it together, you know? Like, I'm just going through the motions, trying to get through each day without completely falling apart. (voice cracking) And it's hard, because I feel like I should be able to handle all of this, but I just don't know if I can. (wiping away tears) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard to talk about this.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, feeling a lump in my throat) Yes... that's been me lately. I've been having a really hard time sleeping, and it's not just because the baby is waking me up all the time. It's like, my mind is racing and I just can't seem to turn it off. I'll lie there in bed, thinking about all the things I need to do, and worrying about the baby, and feeling guilty about not being a good enough mom... (sighing) And it's hard to explain, but it's like I'm just feeling this deep sadness and unhappiness all the time, and it's making it hard for me to relax and fall asleep. (rubbing my eyes) I've been having trouble falling asleep, and then when I do finally fall asleep, I wake up a few hours later and I'm wide awake again. It's like, my body is exhausted, but my mind is still going a million miles an hour. (shaking my head) And it's not just the lack of sleep that's the problem, it's the fact that I'm just feeling so unhappy and overwhelmed all the time. (voice cracking) I feel like I'm just stuck in this rut, and I don't know how to get out of it.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears welling up in my eyes) Yes... that's been me a lot lately. I just feel so sad and miserable all the time. It's like, I'm supposed to be happy and excited about being a new mom, but instead I just feel overwhelmed and anxious and scared. (sighing) I feel like I'm just going through the motions, trying to take care of the baby and do all the things I'm supposed to do, but I'm just not feeling any joy or happiness. (shaking my head) It's like, I'm just existing, not really living. And it's hard, because I feel like I should be feeling happy and grateful for this little baby, but instead I just feel sad and trapped. (voice cracking) I feel like I'm losing myself in all of this, like I'm just disappearing into this role of motherhood and I don't know who I am anymore. (wiping away tears) Sorry, it's just... it's really hard to talk about this. It feels like I'm admitting that I'm a failure or something, that I'm not cut out for this whole mom thing. (looking down, feeling ashamed) But at the same time, it's a relief to finally say it out loud, to finally admit that I'm not okay.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down my face) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start crying. It's not even like I'm thinking about anything sad, it's just like the emotions are just overflowing and I don't know how to stop them. (sobbing) And it's not just when I'm alone, either. I've cried in front of my husband, in front of my family... it's just like I'm not in control of my emotions anymore. (wiping my nose with a tissue) I feel like I'm just so fragile and emotional all the time, and it's really scary. (shaking my head) I don't know how to make it stop, or how to feel better. I just feel like I'm drowning in all these emotions and I don't know how to keep my head above water. (crying uncontrollably) Sorry, I'm just... I'm really sorry. It's just... it's all just too much sometimes. (between sobs) I feel like I'm a good mom, I really do... but sometimes it just feels like everything is too much for me to handle.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(shaking my head) No, I don't think about harming myself. I mean, I feel really overwhelmed and sad a lot of the time, but I don't think about hurting myself. (pausing, looking down) I just feel like I'm not doing a good enough job as a mom, and that's really hard for me to deal with. But I would never want to hurt myself. I just want to be able to take care of my baby and be happy, you know? (sighing) I just feel like I'm struggling to cope with everything right now, but I'm not thinking about harming myself. I just want to find a way to feel better and be a good mom to my baby.

As a new mother, you're experiencing a range of emotions and challenges that are common during the postpartum period, but the intensity and persistence of these feelings suggest that you may be struggling with <med>postpartum depression</med>. It's completely understandable to feel overwhelmed, sad, and anxious, especially when adjusting to the significant changes that come with having a new baby. Your feelings of guilt, self-doubt, and anxiety about being a good mother are valid, and it's essential to acknowledge that you're not alone in this experience.
**Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 24, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include <sym>The patient's response indicates a significant decrease in their ability to laugh and see the funny side of things, stating they've 'lost my sense of humor a bit' and 'it's not the same', which aligns with the option 'Definitely not so much now</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates they have not been looking forward to things and have lost interest in activities they used to enjoy, which aligns with the option 'Hardly at all'.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they blame themselves unnecessarily when things go wrong most of the time, citing various scenarios where they feel at fault, even when trying their best.</sym>, <sym>the 'Yes, very often' option.</sym>, <sym>Patient expresses feeling overwhelmed, like they're 'drowning in responsibility' and 'barely holding it together', indicating a strong difficulty in coping with their situation.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates that they have been experiencing difficulty sleeping due to feelings of unhappiness, which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option, as they mention it's been a consistent issue and describe a deep sadness and unhappiness that's always present.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates feeling sad and miserable most of the time, as they mention it's been their experience 'a lot lately' and describe feeling overwhelmed, anxious, and scared, with no joy or happiness, which aligns with the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>, <sym>The patient's response indicates frequent and uncontrollable crying, even in front of others, and describes feeling overwhelmed by emotions, matching the 'Yes, most of the time' option.</sym>)
**Reasoning:** The patient's responses indicate a high risk for <med>postpartum depression</med>, with persistent feelings of <sym>sadness</sym>, <sym>loss of pleasure</sym>, and <sym>anxiety</sym>. The patient reports difficulty coping with emotions and responsibilities, and <sym>sleep difficulties</sym> linked to mood. According to the EPDS guidelines, a score of 24 indicates probable <med>depression</med>, and urgent referral to a <med>primary care provider (PCP)</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med> is recommended. The patient's symptoms align with the <med>DSM-5 criteria for Major Depressive Disorder with Peripartum Onset</med>, including <sym>depressed mood</sym>, <sym>loss of interest</sym>, <sym>anxiety</sym>, and <sym>sleep disturbances</sym>. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
**Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:**
1. Arrange urgent appointment with <med>PCP</med> or <med>mental health specialist</med>
2. Encourage <med>sleep hygiene practices</med> to improve sleep quality
3. Recommend <med>stress management techniques</med>, such as deep breathing, meditation, or yoga
4. Support patient in connecting with local <med>postpartum support groups</med> or online resources
5. Encourage patient to share feelings and concerns with partner, family, and friends to build a support network
Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
